topic: Electronic beam steering for satellite links
scope: Generic conceptual demonstration of one satellite carrying an electronically steered phased array; not a model of a named satellite or a claim about every LEO system.

captions.support: LEO satellite-to-ground geometry changes during a pass.
The direction from a moving satellite to a fixed ground terminal changes.
The array elements contribute coherently, with relative phase controlled.

captions.text: Shift the phase. Steer the beam.
captions.support: A progressive phase change moves the main lobe within the available scan range.

captions.text: Keep the beam on the terminal.
captions.support: Conceptual electronic pointing during part of a pass, not an end-to-end link guarantee.

voiceover: A satellite moves across the sky, and the direction to a ground terminal keeps changing. A phased array can steer its main beam without rotating the antenna panel. Each element contributes a radio wave. Change the relative phase, and those waves add most strongly in a new direction. The result is electronic pointing, within the antenna’s scan range. Real arrays still have sidelobes and losses.

formula.array: Ideal narrowband uniform linear array, elements at x_n = n d; inspect the x–z plane.
formula.angle_convention: theta is measured from the panel normal (+z); positive theta tilts toward +x.
formula.phasor_convention: Time dependence exp(+i omega t), outward propagation exp(-i k r).
formula.steering_weights: w_n = exp(-i k n d sin(theta_0))
formula.array_factor: AF(theta) = (1/N) sum[n=0..N-1] exp(i n k d [sin(theta)-sin(theta_0)])
formula.source_note: Analog Devices derives the adjacent path difference d sin(theta) and the phase-shift magnitude. The signed transmit expression here is derived under the explicit phasor convention; another convention may flip the sign without changing the physics.

animation_rules: Keep the array panel mechanically fixed to the satellite while changing the main-beam direction relative to that panel.
Show all elements radiating simultaneously. Phase offset is not switching individual elements on in sequence.
On a small array inset, show same-phase emission at broadside and a phase ramp for an off-normal direction.
A 30-degree example with half-wavelength spacing needs a 90-degree phase-step magnitude.
Treat cone, rings, beam footprint, orbital speed, sizes, and timing as visual explanation. Do not present them as RF measurements or an orbital simulation.
A line or translucent cone indicates the main-beam pointing direction; it does not depict all radiated power.
If showing a normalized pattern, use the array factor consistently and retain sidelobes; do not label a single cone as the full radiation pattern.
must_not_claim: All LEO satellites or every terminal use the same antenna architecture.
No spacecraft motion, attitude control, or mechanical setup is ever needed.
Arbitrary 360-degree steering from one planar aperture, unlimited scan range, or equal gain at every angle.
Zero sidelobes, zero losses, or the absence of grating lobes for arbitrary element spacing.
A fixed phase shift steers every frequency to exactly the same angle.
Instantaneous, lossless, or interruption-free handover; RF pointing alone does not establish that.
Specific throughput, latency, altitude, wavelength, element count, tracking accuracy, or switching time for a commercial constellation without specific evidence.
The sample demonstrates a tested RF system or physically accurate propagation timing.
